newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says to maintain import ban on Taiwan pork.
newsitem.headline: Japan says to maintain import ban on Taiwan pork.

text.p: Japan will maintain its ban on imports of Taiwanese pork despite Taiwan's decision to lift an export ban imposed last month over an outbreak of hog disease, a senior Agriculture Ministry official said on Thursday.
"Our stance is unchanged. We're going to maintain a ban on all imports of pork from Taiwan indefinitely," said Akinori Aonuma, director of the ministry's animal health division.
"It is not possible to allow any shipments of Taiwanese pork to Japan at the moment," Aonuma said.
Taiwan said earlier on Thursday it had lifted an export ban on pork that it had imposed on March 20 due to an outbreak of highly contagious foot-and-mouth disease there.
But officials at Taiwan's Agriculture Council said exporters must first obtain permits from importing countries.
On March 21, Japan imposed an indefinite ban on all pork imports from Taiwan, its largest supplier, due to the outbreak.
Japan is the largest export market for Taiwanese pork. It imported 653,176 tonnes of pork in 1996, according to Finance Ministry data. Of that, 266,225 tonnes, or 40.7 percent, came from Taiwan.
